in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're looking after, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm looking after my son Alex. He's 8 years old. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You're looking after your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and living arrangements with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you contributing financially towards his care (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. And to be honest, I'm not currently contributing financially to his care at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your situation. This is important information.

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently contributing financially to his care, I need to ask:

**Is someone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, the person he lives with)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

To qualify for Child Benefit, you need to be considered "responsible" for the child. Under the rules, you're usually responsible for a child if either:
1. You live with them, OR
2. You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money

Since Alex lives with your ex-partner and you're not currently making financial contributions towards his care, you don't meet either of these criteria.

**Important to note:** Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex lives with your ex-partner, they would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for him (if they haven't already).

However, if your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you start making regular financial contributions towards Alex's care that equal or exceed the Child Benefit amount - you may be able to claim then. If that happens, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.
